abstract: Adding a second source acquisition cohort improved recognition of the weaker motor-imagery class in an external electroencephalographic evaluation. We tested source-cohort expansion as a data-design strategy using nine BNCI participants alone, those nine plus 20 Yang participants, and the nine plus all 51 Yang participants. Two EEGNet input pipelines and eight source-only checkpoint rules were evaluated under a common 5,120-update full-trajectory budget; common-duration controls used 2,560 updates. The experiment comprised 108 neural trajectories and nine conventional spatial-filtering fits, with exploratory external evaluation in 85 Dreyer participants. In the prespecified broadband/tail-recall comparison, expansion from nine to 60 source participants increased weaker-class recall from 27.31% to 48.48%: +21.17 percentage points (95% confidence interval 17.12–25.21; paired p<0.001). Balanced accuracy increased by 5.85 points (95% confidence interval 4.13–7.58; Holm-adjusted p<0.001). Weaker-class recall improved in 72/85 participants; an additional descriptive analysis found simultaneous improvement in both endpoints in 66/85. The mean absolute class-recall gap narrowed from 62.01 to 31.38 points, a 49.39% reduction. At the common 20-epoch checkpoint, weaker-class gains were 17.07 and 24.87 points in the broadband and shared-view pipelines. Supplementary post hoc analyses also identified gains in the fixed intermediate source pool and the conventional decoder. Source-cohort expansion therefore improved weaker-command coverage and overall discrimination in the evaluated cross-dataset setting. The study combines controlled source composition, matched-duration checks and participant-level benefit profiles to establish a reproducible empirical strategy for improving cross-subject decoding.
introduction:
Adding a second acquisition cohort improved cross-subject motor-imagery EEG decoding: in the primary external comparison, weaker-class recall rose by 21.17 percentage points and balanced accuracy by 5.85 points. The weaker-class gain extended to 72 of 85 evaluated participants, and the mean left–right recall gap nearly halved. These findings address a practical requirement of two-command decoding: useful performance depends on recognizing the less accurately decoded command as well as achieving a high average score. EEG classification reviews and reproducible cross-dataset benchmarks provide the methodological foundation for evaluating these complementary outcomes [1,2].

The study's principal contribution is a controlled evaluation of source-cohort expansion as a decoder-design choice. Three nested source pools separate the BNCI-only configuration from two mixed-cohort configurations, each under the same full-trajectory update budget. Matched-duration checkpoint comparisons then test whether the gains remain when selected training duration is also fixed. Joint participant-level endpoints distinguish improvements shared by the same people from improvements appearing only in separate cohort averages. A common-channel, trial-wise dimensionless processing contract connects these comparisons across recording systems. Together, these elements make the observed improvement attributable to a documented source-configuration change rather than an unspecified change in the decoding pipeline.

Recent domain-generalization methods learn transferable EEG representations through contrastive regularization, marginal and conditional alignment, and latent-distribution exploration with feature fusion [3–5]. Source-population design complements these approaches: the training population determines which recorded variations are available, while checkpoint selection determines the deployed state. Established work on model-selection bias and brain-decoder evaluation motivates keeping these decisions within source data [6,7]. Domain-generalization benchmarks treat selection as part of the evaluated pipeline [8], and EEG protocol research emphasizes participant partitions and random initialization [9]. Our design extends this framework to the combined effects of source expansion, weaker-command coverage and participant-level benefit under explicitly controlled training budgets.

We used an established EEGNet backbone [10] and conventional common spatial patterns (CSP) with linear discriminant analysis (LDA) [11] to evaluate the source-design strategy across two decoding approaches. The objective was to determine whether adding Yang recordings to a BNCI source pool improved external weaker-class recall and balanced accuracy, and whether these gains persisted at a common selected duration. The completed comparisons supported both improvements; the following analyses quantify their size, distribution and dependence on the evaluated configuration.
discussion:
### Source-cohort expansion as an effective decoder-design choice

The principal result is a 21.17-point increase in external weaker-class recall alongside a 5.85-point increase in balanced accuracy. This combination improves recognition of the less-recognized command while increasing overall discrimination. The added participant-level analysis sharpens that result: 66 of 85 people improved on both endpoints simultaneously, and 72 improved on weaker-class recall. Thus, the two positive cohort averages also represent concurrent gains for most evaluated participants. The practical contribution is a reproducible source-design change that can be assessed alongside representation learning and model selection.

Full neural trajectories received 5,120 updates at every source level. Adding Yang changed the dataset sampling mass from BNCI-only to equal BNCI/Yang weighting. The common epoch-20 comparisons provide the key duration control: source expansion improved both endpoints at the same 2,560 selected updates within each pipeline. The benefit therefore remained present when selected duration was held fixed, strengthening the source-configuration interpretation. This distinction is important because the primary source-only rule selected different durations across source pools.

### Consistency across source configurations and decoding approaches

The fixed intermediate source pool reached 49.03% weaker-class recall, with a supplementary S29−S9 estimate of +21.72 points. This identifies a concrete mixed-source configuration in which substantial improvement was already present. The source roster, eligible-trial inventory and selected checkpoint are supplied, enabling direct reproduction and later tests of alternative source subsets.

The conventional CSP–LDA decoder also gained 13.82 points in weaker-class recall and 5.25 points in balanced accuracy from S9 to S60. Source-expansion benefits therefore occurred in both the compact neural and spatial-filtering approaches evaluated here. Large-scale MOABB benchmarking similarly highlights training-data availability and the importance of strong conventional comparators [21]. At a common neural checkpoint duration, all three fitted seeds showed positive cohort-mean changes in both pipelines and both endpoints. These complementary comparisons support the source-design result across several evaluated configurations on the same external cohort.

### Class rebalancing explains the coverage gain

The identity B=W+|rL−rR|/2 relates average discrimination to weaker-class coverage and recall asymmetry. In the primary comparison, the mean absolute recall gap decreased by 30.63 points, or 49.39%; it narrowed in 72 of 85 participants. This explains why the numerical increase in weaker-class recall was much larger than the increase in balanced accuracy. The decoder's operating profile became more balanced, with more recognition capacity directed toward the previously under-recognized command. Reporting both endpoints and their paired participant changes makes this behavior visible.

The contribution complements domain-generalization representation learning [3–5] through explicit source-design and checkpoint-selection accounting. The common 18-channel processing contract and trial-wise normalization provide a reproducible numerical basis across cohorts, while held-out source curves, frozen choices and saved external predictions connect the design to its measured effects. This evaluation pattern supports comparison of future source populations without making architecture ranking the central claim.

### Scope and next validation

The evidence concerns complete source configurations in one exploratory external cohort, one fixed intermediate subset and three fitted seeds. Expansion changes cohort composition, trial availability and sampling frequency together; matched-duration controls address duration, not these other components. Rebalancing included increased right-hand recall and decreased left-hand recall, and ten participants had lower weaker-class recall. The prespecified selector and S60−S29 contrasts remain uncertain, while tail-cross-entropy selection produced adverse expansion effects; all are retained in Table 2 and the complete supporting tables. Accordingly, the study establishes the observed source-configuration benefit rather than universal selector superiority, monotonic sample-size gains or uniformly improved hand-specific recall. Yang timing/unit conventions and feedback-containing task windows define the signal scope. Independent acquisition cohorts and prospectively varied source subsets are the next validation steps.
conclusions: Source-cohort expansion increased weaker-class recall by 21.17 percentage points and balanced accuracy by 5.85 points in the primary 85-person external comparison. Sixty-six participants improved on both endpoints, and the mean class-recall gap nearly halved. Benefits were also present at equal-duration checkpoints, in the fixed intermediate source pool and in the conventional decoder. These results establish a concrete source-design strategy for improving weaker-command recognition in the evaluated cross-dataset setting, supported by controlled update budgets, complementary decoding approaches and an auditable participant-level record.

# Cover letter

Dear PLOS ONE Editorial Office,

Please advise on consideration of the substantially revised Research Article, **“Source-cohort expansion improves weaker-class coverage in cross-subject motor-imagery EEG decoding.”**

The study evaluates a practical data-design strategy: expanding the source acquisition cohort while holding the full neural-trajectory update budget fixed. A common 18-channel processing contract, source-only checkpoint selection and equal-duration controls support an external comparison in 85 participants. Relative to the nine-person source pool, the 60-person configuration improved weaker-class recall by 21.17 percentage points (95% CI 17.12–25.21) and balanced accuracy by 5.85 points. Sixty-six participants improved on both endpoints. Improvements were also present at common-duration checkpoints and in a conventional spatial-filtering decoder.

The contribution complements existing domain-generalization algorithms by quantifying how source composition changes participant-level class coverage. The complete experiment comprises 108 neural trajectories and nine conventional fits. Code, full saved predictions, all protocol-specified contrasts and supplementary descriptive analyses are supplied. The external evaluation is identified as exploratory.

**Previous interaction:** an earlier version, PONE-D-26-50597, submitted on 9 October 2026, was rejected on 12 October 2026 because it was simultaneously under consideration elsewhere. I acknowledged this error and on 12 October asked whether a substantially revised version could be considered in future. This package is not presented as an invited revision or as an update to a manuscript still under review. Please confirm the appropriate route for considering this substantive extension. I understand and will comply with the requirement for exclusive consideration.

The manuscript includes the author-confirmed institutional exemption statement for secondary public-data research, provider attribution, data availability and disclosure of AI assistance. I suggest assignment to an Academic Editor with expertise in EEG decoding and reproducible machine learning; I have no opposed reviewers to declare.

Thank you for your guidance and consideration.

Sincerely,

Ziyuan Zhu, sole and corresponding author  
College of Artificial Intelligence Medicine, Chongqing Medical University, Chongqing, China  
zzy2630816871@gmail.com

captions.1: **Fig 1. Source-expansion design and evidence flow.** **A**, Nested S9/S29/S60 source pools contain 9/29/60 participants and 2,592/14,590/33,183 eligible trials. **B**, One 18-channel, trial-wise dimensionless transform supplies the spectral inputs. **C–D**, Five participant-held-out folds, three validation seeds and three final seeds produce 90 validation trajectories, 18 final trajectories and 48 checkpoint choices. Full trajectories receive 5,120 updates; 144 evaluated outputs reuse 99 distinct checkpoints. **E**, External scoring uses 85 Dreyer participants and 6,800 trials. **F**, Archived checks link input identities, source selections and prediction statistics. Source data: `figure_data/Fig1_source_configurations.csv`; audit scope: S1 Appendix.
captions.2: **Fig 2. All four prespecified participant-paired contrasts.** The filled circle shows the primary 21.17-point weaker-class-recall gain from S9 to S60 under BROAD/tail-recall selection. Open squares show all three secondary contrasts. Points average 85 paired participant differences after within-participant averaging across three final seeds. Bars are pointwise 95% t intervals. The primary p value is unadjusted; secondary p values use one Holm family. Source data: `figure_data/neural_recomputed_comparisons.csv`.
captions.3: **Fig 3. Participant-level improvement in weaker-class recall.** Bars show all 85 S60−S9 BROAD/tail-recall changes in ascending order: 72 improvements, ten declines and three ties. The dashed line marks the mean increase of 21.17 points. Metrics are calculated within seed, then averaged across three seeds within participant. Participant identifiers and plot order are retained in `figure_data/Fig3_primary_participant_changes.csv`. Joint changes in both endpoints are provided in S4 Data.
captions.4: **Fig 4. Class coverage and balanced accuracy across source configurations.** **A**, Balanced accuracy; **B**, weaker-class recall; **C**, mean absolute class-recall gap. Neural rows use source-only tail-recall selection; CSP–LDA uses the fixed comparator configuration. A/B show participant means and pointwise 95% t intervals (n=85). C is the descriptive decomposition `2 × (balanced accuracy − weaker-class recall)`. For BROAD, the gap falls from 62.01 to 31.38 points, a 49.39% reduction. Lines guide the eye. Source data: `figure_data/Fig4_descriptive_endpoints.csv` and `figure_data/Fig4_posthoc_absolute_recall_gap.csv`.
captions.5: **Fig 5. All 48 source-only checkpoint choices.** The matrix shows eight selection rules across three source pools and two neural pipelines. Numbers indicate the epoch applied to all three final seeds. The outlined primary BROAD/tail-recall cells select epochs 27, 5 and 5 for S9, S29 and S60. Each full trajectory contains 40 epochs × 128 updates; evaluation uses its rule-specific checkpoint. Source data: `figure_data/Fig5_selected_epochs.csv` and the frozen selection record.
captions.6: **Fig 6. Supplementary post hoc source-expansion comparisons.** S29−S9 BROAD/tail-recall gains are 21.72 points for weaker-class recall and 5.79 points for balanced accuracy; corresponding S60−S9 CSP–LDA gains are 13.82 and 5.25 points. All four contrasts were specified after the original outcomes were known and use the same 85 participants with three-seed within-participant averages. Bars are pointwise 95% t intervals; displayed p values use a separate four-test Holm family. Source data: `figure_data/Fig6_review2_posthoc_comparisons.csv`.
captions.7: **Fig 7. Source-expansion gains at a common 20-epoch checkpoint.** **A**, Balanced accuracy; **B**, weaker-class recall. Bars display all S29−S9 and S60−S9 mean changes in BROAD and shared-view pipelines at 20 epochs and 2,560 updates. The 24 points show three seed-specific cohort-mean differences for every expansion/pipeline/endpoint combination; all are positive. This duration-matched descriptive control uses the same 85 external participants. The complete 68-contrast inventory, including negative outcomes under other rules, is retained in `figure_data/Fig7_complete_source_expansion_inventory.csv`; seed data: `figure_data/Fig7_fixed20_seed_differences.csv`.
